messages:
Samir: FYI customer (NexGen Health) asked for a pricing proposal — 4mo reserved GPU pool with ability to shift unused capacity into next-month burst credits (carryover up to 30%). They want a blended per-token number vs pure reserved + overage. Can product/finance advise? cc @Anya
Anya: Quick clarifying q: is 'shift' = carryover credits or flexible reallocation across months? Also need expected tokens/month and target blended delta to size the ask for backlog.
Samir: They mean carryover credits (not pooled across contracts). Expect ~120B tokens/mo baseline, spike to ~200B in month 3. They'd like a blended rate ~20% below our list reserved price over the 4mo horizon.
Jamie: Finance note — carryover affects revenue treatment but we can model it as a short-lived credit pool. Rough sketch: reserved commit priced at discount D, unused portion up to 30% becomes 'Burst Credits' for next calendar month; burst beyond credits billed at overage multiplier M (roughly 1.5x-1.8x). Need exact numbers to produce blended.
Leo: Eng constraints: prefer implementing carryover as a billing-level credit (simple) vs dynamic routing between reserved pools (complex). Billing credits avoid routing changes, but we need console UX for credit visibility + a redemption check in the billing pipeline.
Anya: Proposed launch criteria for this feature: 1) signed contract language for carryover credits, 2) finance-approved blended-rate model and revenue note, 3) console shows credit balance and expiration, 4) SLO definition for burst (95th <250ms), 5) doc for sales on quoting. If any missing, punt to backlog refinement.
Samir: Customer asked for a sample clause to include in the contract. Jamie, can you paste a short one?
Jamie: ```If Customer consumes less than 100% of their Reserved Capacity in a given month, up to 30% of the unused Reserved Capacity will convert into "Burst Credits" redeemable during the following calendar month. Burst Credits expire at the end of that month. Burst usage beyond available Burst Credits will be billed at applicable overage rates.```
Billing Bot: Current public rate card: https://redwood.ai/docs/rate-card. Internal packaging model: https://internal.redwood/packaging/model-312 (view-perms required). Current baseline: reserved list = $X per 1M tokens; typical overage multiplier ~1.7x.
Anya: Triage decision: add a 'pricing-packaging: carryover credits' ticket to backlog and scope as a medium-priority initiative. @Leo please estimate eng effort for the soft-credit path; @Jamie assign finance owner for the blended model.
Leo: Estimate for soft-credit implementation: ~2w eng (billing + console) + 1w SRE validation, small docs. Hard routing solution would be 4-6w. Soft-credit recommended.
Samir: Great — I'll message the customer with the proposed approach and a ~3wk timeline for a formal draft. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
